comments.author: mglyn
comments.body: I added the request-scoped Cache-DiT refresh hint in this PR (extra_params.force_refresh_step_hint, with an optional once/repeat policy). Keeping it together with the quality switch is intentional: both features control the same per-request Cache-DiT lifecycle and share the same policy/runtime path. The change remains H3-scoped, while other models retain their existing behavior by default.

comments.author: david6666666
comments.body:
Single-GPU sanity check (B300 x1, 1344x768, 5s/124 frames, 50 steps, seed 1101, FLASH_ATTN, eager, FL2VA t2va): main @ a874b8e0 vs PR head 7a94a444.

| config | elapsed | vs lossless |
|---|---|---|
| main (reference, no cache) | 157.4s | -- |
| quality=lossless (no cache) | 153.4s | -- |
| quality=lossless (server started with cache_dit) | 158.8s | -- |
| quality=omitted (cache_dit startup, generic profile) | 100.7s | -34% |
| quality=high | 96.3s | -37% |

Precision:
- lossless vs main baseline: frames + audio bit-identical (max diff 0) -- reference path is exactly aligned with main.
- lossless on a cache_dit server vs plain lossless: bit-identical -- the uninstall path leaves no hooks behind.
- high vs main: SSIM 0.778 / PSNR 21.7 dB on this single-GPU workload, lower than the 0.97 / 33-41 dB reported for 4xL20X SP4. The cache hits more aggressively here (~1.59x vs the claimed ~1.35x), so the quality/throughput tradeoff shifts with deployment.

The mechanism (routing + batch isolation + request-scoped lifecycle) checks out; the lossless path is a faithful reference and the perf gain is real. The high quality numbers look deployment-dependent rather than universal.

Our high request selects a fixed Cache-DiT profile, but its actual hit rate and speed/quality tradeoff are deployment-dependent. We intentionally do not gate it by GPU, topology, or request shape; lossless remains the exact reference path. I updated the PR text to scope the reported metrics to our 4×L20X SP4 experiment and avoid a universal guarantee. Thanks for the additional validation.
